ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 3
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Punctuation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Punctuation.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Punctuation.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Punctuation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Punctuation.

2. When practising Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Spelling.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Spelling.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Spelling.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Spelling.

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

4. When practising Attentive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening.

5. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.

6. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.

7. When practising Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Guided Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Guided Writing.

8. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.

9. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.

10. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

11. When practising Language Activities at home, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Activities at home.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Language Activities at home.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Language Activities at home.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Activities at home.

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. blue
   C. happiness
   D. quickly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Punctuation.

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Spelling.

3. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening.

5. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Writing.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

10. A — One main idea with supporting sentences

11. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Activities at home.

12. A — run

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Attentive Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Word Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
